items.title: Beetle Imaging Procedure
items.text: Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Imaging Pinned Ground Beetles at the NEON Biorepository.

items.title: Purpose and Scope
items.text: This SOP provides detailed protocols for imaging pinned ground beetle specimens at the NEON Biorepository. It incorporates computer vision-friendly techniques to maximize the scientific value of digitized specimens both for human interpretation and automated analysis.

items.title: Required Equipment
items.text:
Use the following checklist to keep track of materials collected.

Materials Checklist
- [ ] Header Box  
    - [ ] Cm scale ruler  
    - [ ] Color calibration chart  
    - [ ] Standardized labels (domain, year, species, expert IDed or not)  
    - [ ] Unit trays  
    - [ ] Pen  
    - [ ] Insect pins for propping up the labels to pinned specimen height  
- [ ] Computer with metadata spreadsheet template# (1)!
    - [ ] Supplemental–Template  
    - [ ] Google Drive for photo backups (Link to Your Drive here)
        - [ ] Email [email of person managing drive] if you need access to the Google Drive  
- [ ] Digital camera with appropriate lens  
    - [ ] Macro lens (for small beetles)  
- [ ] Light diffusers and controlled lighting setup
  1. Make a copy of the Metadata Spreadsheet Template in your project Drive.

items.title: Purpose and Scope
items.text: This SOP provides detailed protocols for checking the CSV files of trays where the data processing query has identified too many or too few individuals for the Tray.

items.title: Too Many Individuals: "QueryOver”
items.text:
• Enter the directory “NEONIndividualLinkageChecks/QueryOver” to see what needs to be checked.
  • Order the folder alphabetically by Name to group species together
  • For each csv in the folder:
  • Open the csv file
  • Click the “open with” drop-down at the top of the screen and select Google Sheets
  • Use the File Name (species, year, domain, tray type, ID range) to locate the physical tray of specimens
  • There will be a blank column next to “individualID” called “Present”, this is where you will enter your information.
  • Carefully compare the list of individualID’s in the CSV with those in the tray.
    • Enter a 1 into “Present” if the beetle is in the tray, enter a 0 if it is absent
  • Once all of the rows have a 0 or a 1, do a check by enter =SUM([interst cells here]) at the bottom of the column
    • This will likely autofill with cell values if the data has all be entered
  • Compare the SUM value to the value in column “NumberOfBeetlesInTray”
  • Ensure that it matches and DELETE THE EQUATION
  • Close the file and move both the csv and the google sheet into the folder “Checked”
  • Repeat for all files until the folder is empty and everything has been moved to “Checked”

items.title: Too Few Individuals: "QueryUnder”
items.text:
• Enter the directory “NEONIndividualLinkageChecks/QueryUnder” to see what needs to be checked.
  • Order the folder alphabetically by Name to group species together
  • For each csv in the folder:
  • Open the csv file
  • Click the “open with” drop-down at the top of the screen and select Google Sheets
  • Use the File Name (species, year, domain, tray type, ID range) to locate the physical tray of specimens
  • There will be two blank columns next to “individualID” called “Present” and “Order”, this is where you will enter your information.
  • Carefully compare the list of individualID’s in the CSV with those in the tray.
    • Enter a 1 into “Present” if the beetle is in the tray, enter a 0 if it is absent
    • For 1’s, enter their order in the box, as displayed below.
  • When you find a beetle with an individualID that is not in the spreadsheet, insert a row and carefully transcribe the full individualID number from the beetle, enter a 1 in present, and record its order in the box.
  • Once all of the rows have a 0 or a 1, do a check by enter =SUM([interst cells here]) at the bottom of the column
    • This will likely autofill with cell values if the data has all be entered
  • Compare the SUM value to the value in column “NumberOfBeetlesInTray”
  • Ensure that it matches and DELETE THE EQUATION
  • Close the file and move both the csv and the google sheet into the folder “Checked”
  • Repeat for all files until the folder is empty and everything has been moved to “Checked”

items.title: Other things that can happen:
items.text: • Sometimes the query is incorrect because the number of beetles in the tray was counted or recorded incorrectly. If you find that the number in “NumberOfBeetlesInTray” is incorrect, update it the column

items.title: Setup Preparation
items.text:
• Clean all equipment and work surfaces.
  • Arrange diffuse lighting to minimize shadows and glare.
  • Turn on lights.
  • Put batteries in flashes and turn them on.

items.title: Lightroom - Camera Tethering
items.text:
• Turn on the Camera.
  • Open Lightroom on the desktop.
  • Link the Camera to Lightroom with tethering:
    • File/Teathering/Start Teathering
  • Ensure that destination is “C:\Users\biorepository\Desktop\Beetle Tray Pics\BTray\ABTrays`:
  • A control bar will open on the screen: Open Live view to look at the camera view on the computer screen:

items.title: Camera Settings
items.text:
• Ensure the camera is in Manual (M) mode:
  • Ensure that the lens is set to focus:
  • Ensure the camera is set to manual focus.
  • Adjust camera aperature settings from live view:
    • Use aperture settings that maximize depth of field (f/8-f/11) (Different for small beetles).
    • Use ISO settings that minimize noise (ISO 100-400) (recommendation, see what works for your setup).
    • Shutter Speeds for this camera generally work around 100-200, but it will depend on the species and ambient lighting.

items.title: File Storage and Redundant Backup
items.text:
• Save images using the default naming convention on the camera and record names in the metadata sheet for automated renaming.
    • This reduces the chance of mistranscription.
  • Store images in at least two separate locations (primary storage and sharing).

    • Locally on the Computer, Google Drive, and OSC.

      • Google Drive is copied to OSC regularly with the following shell script. Replace <PROJECT-CODE> with your project code. The local directory should be set based on the HPC system used.
      #!/bin/bash

# Exit if any command fails
set -e

# Set remote name and path
REMOTE="GoogleDrive_NEONBeetle2"

# Set local destination
LOCAL_DIR="/fs/ess/<PROJECT-CODE>/CarabidImaging/" 

# Use rclone to copy only new or updated files
rclone copy "$REMOTE:" "$LOCAL_DIR" \
--drive-export-formats xlsx \
--update \
--verbose \
--exclude "*/Student/" \
--log-file="$LOCAL_DIR/rclone_sync.log"

items.title: Data Exports
items.text:
• Locate the raw images in the computer's file system: C:\Users\biorepository\Desktop\Beetle Tray Pics\BTray\ABTrays\ABTrays-NEONBiorepository\
  • Select all of the Raw photos (.CR3 files) and copy them to the Google Drive in the folder /Images/Raw/.
  • In Lightroom, select all photos from the date of imaging
    • Click the grid view (looks like a grid of boxes at the bottom left of the interface): and use Shift + click to select all images of interest
  • Right-click on selected images and select “Export”:
  • Export as PNG (This export takes a while).
    • Ensure that the PPI is assigned to 300:
    • Don’t modify the names
    • Export in the folder: C:\\Users\\biorepository\\Desktop\\Beetle Tray Pics\\BTray\\ABTrays\\ABTrays-NEONBiorepository\\PNGs
  • Once the export is done, select all PNGs and upload them to the Google Drive in the folder /Images/PNG/

items.title: Metadata
items.text:
Metadata for each image needs to be transcribed into a spreadsheet in addition to being in the photo itself. Use BeetleMetadata1 (column values defined on ColumnNames tab). Each image will constitute a row in the spreadsheet with a column to include:

  • imageID - copy and paste this from light lightroom
  • First two "individualIDs" and last 2 "individualIDs" in the tray (This is necessary for redundancy in case of mistranscription. If one ID is incorrect, the whole photo could be rendered unusable.)
    • In the metadata google sheets I have embedded a lot of conditional formatting so that there are visual cues of problems
      • red cells: the IndividualID is the wrong length
      • orange cells: IndividualID_1 when IndividualID_n is numerically lower than IndividualID_1, eg the box is out of order
  • Number of individuals in the tray (NumberOfBeetles).
  • Marked: Record “yes” once the header label of the unit tray has been marked with a pen to denote that imaging has occurred
  • checkedOrder: Record “yes” once you have ensured that all individualIDs are sequential.
  • Expert or paratax box (Must be explicitly labeled one way, not left blank).

  • scientificName

    Success

    ExpertOrPara, domainID, and importantly scientificName are all formatted as defined ranges that reference lists of real values (such as the species list, pulled from the API) so that there can't be any spelling errors and appear as drop downs that can be typed in, but will not fill it they are invalid values.

  • domainID

  • Photographer
  • DatePhotographed

  1. Copy this Metadata Spreadsheet Template to your Drive or use the xlsx version provided in the GitHub repo. ↩

items.title: C Tray Beetle
items.text:
Warning

Placing two C trays in a single image is not recommended. Ultimately, this workflow created more hassels downstream than time saved in imaging.

items.title: Required Elements in Each Image
items.text:
• Separate Header tray for each C tray with:
    • Place cm scale in same focal plane as specimens.
    • Include color calibration chart in each image.
    • Include domain label visible in frame.
    • Ensure species label is clearly visible.
    • Include expert or parataxonomist label.
  • Both C trays should be of similarly sized species so that they are all in focus. When in doubt, do only one tray at a time.

items.title: Image Capture
items.text:
• Zoom into an individual beetle with the magnifying glass on the bottom right of the touch screen.
  • Manually focus on the specimen.
  • Focus carefully on the top of the specimens, not labels or pins.
  • Move the zoom box to check the specimens in the other tray are also in focus.
  • Take test shot and review for proper exposure, focus, and framing.
  • Ensure all required elements are visible in frame.
  • Capture final image and verify quality before proceeding.
    • To verify, zoom in on individual beetle to ensure it is clear and in focus, see example photos.

items.title: Metadata
items.text:
Because C Trays are imaged two at a time, there is a separate C Tray Template; the column values are defined on the ColumnNames Sheet:

  • Mark: Record “yes” once the header label of the unit tray has been marked with a pen to denote that imaging has occurred.
  • All of the column are the same as the A and B Trays, but there are twice as many columns, with Tray1_ or Tray2_ appended to the beginning of the column names to enter data for both trays in a single image (e.g., Tray_1_IndividualID_1).
    • If there is ever just one Tray in the image, enter it into Tray1_ columns, and put NA in to the Tray2_ columns.
  • In some cases, you will not have 4 beetles for the individual ID records, in this case do the following:
    • 1 Beetle: Record the IndividualID in IndividualID_1 and enter NA to other columns.
    • 2 Beetles: Record the IndividualID in IndividualID_1 and IndividualID_n and enter NA the middle columns (this is very important for querying).
    • 1 Beetles: Record the IndividualIDs in IndividualID_1, IndividualID_2 and IndividualID_n and enter NA the middle column (this is very important for querying).

items.title: Specimen Arrangement
items.text:
• FIRST CHECK: If beetles are on paper points, use the Small Beetle Protocol.
  • Position beetles with consistent orientation in the tray.
  • Position specimens in center of frame to minimize lens distortion.
  • Check that specimens are in sequential order based on individual ID #.
  • **After imaging, mark the Upper right-hand corner of the unit tray header label**.

items.title: Equipment Setup
items.text:
• Use a camera and macro lens with appropriate magnification:
    • Canon EOS DSLR (model 7D).
    • 24–105 mm macro lens.
  • Use B Tray for rearranging A Trays where necessary.
  • External flashes.
  • Defusion paper, in a cone that extends from camera lens to table around tray (ref photo).

items.title: Specimen Staging
items.text:
• Only B and C Trays allow for appropriate magnification.
  • Include a scale bar in bottom right of the container:
    • This is where there is most likely to be room to add in a scale bar, because of way beetles are arranged from top to bottom left to right.
  • Ensure that the scale bar is level with the beetles, and that all beetles are level with each other (in a single focal plane).
    • This is essential to measuring the size of the beetles, if the scale bar is above or below the beetles in height, the measurement will not be correct.
  • ensure beetles are sequentially based on individual ID numbers.
  • Maintain consistent orientation for all specimens.
  • Ensure that beetles are not on the edges of the photo to prevent distortion and poor focus. See example of poor focus: tray of small pinned beetles. The beetle in the top left of the image is surrounded by a black box with a diagonal line to a larger black box taking up most of the image, which is the beetle zoomed in and it is not in focus: gently fuzzy, particularly around the extremities and antennae. The text on the label pinned below the specimen is clearly out of focus

items.title: Image Capture
items.text:
• Zoom into an individual beetle with the magnifying glass on the bottom right of the touch screen.
  • Manually focus on the specimen.
  • Use an F-stop of 5.6.
    • A lower f stop decreases the depth of field, and makes the label more blurry, allowing for segmentation of the beetle from the underlying text.
  • Center the beetles in the images.
  • Ensure the scale bare is not on the very edge of the photo (avoid distortion).
  • Use flashes on TTL (automatic).
    • Ensure exposure looks good in the final image.

items.title: Metadata for Small Beetles
items.text:
For small beetles there is a separate sheet in the metadata sheet called “SmallBeetles” (column values defined on ColumnNames Sheet):

  • Mark: Record “yes” once the header label of the unit tray has been marked with a pen to denote that imaging has occurred.
  • If beetles need to be temporarily moved from an A Tray to a B Tray for imaging, record B under trayType add “From A tray” to the notes column, if they are permanently moved to a B tray, no note is necessary.
  • In some cases, you will not have 4 beetles for the individual ID records, in this case do the following:
    • 1 Beetle: Record the IndividualID in IndividualID_1 and enter NA to other columns.
    • 2 Beetles: Record the IndividualID in IndividualID_1 and IndividualID_n and enter NA the middle columns (this is very important for querying).
    • 1 Beetles: Record the IndividualIDs in IndividualID_1, IndividualID_2 and IndividualID_n and enter NA the middle column (this is very important for querying).
